title: Bind JetBrains approval to the rendered plan
description: Objective: close PlanReviewDialog's stale-render hole using the landed JetBrains model/wire child task-0ad3744e77bd43b08b9c0b63293912a6. Deliverable: freeze a valid reviewed plan revision only after initial DoD/steps render; on a changed revision latch Approve disabled with a localized 'Plan changed - close and reopen to review' notice rather than partially re-rendering the plan. onState must invalidate before the comments-equality return and before the 200ms comment debounce; missing task, non-AWAITING_APPROVAL status, invalid revision and disconnected service cannot approve. The action must independently recheck getState()/isConnected() against the captured revision, but must never substitute the cache's newer revision. Use a production-used headless presenter/state helper in a new src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewApprovalState.kt plus new src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewApprovalStateTest.kt; existing files are toolwindow/PlanReviewDialog.kt and src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties (4 files total). Disable repeated sends while approval pending. Keep dialog open on send failure or daemon APPROVE_TASK error, show the existing onError message without treating transport success as approval; only observed authoritative state may finish an approval. EDT-safe callbacks, stopped debounce timers and removed listener on disposal are mandatory. NOT in scope: rewriting all board/detail approval routes, in-place mutation stamping policy, or VS Code. Tests cover new revision with identical comments, same-revision comment update, forced action while disabled, stale/deleted/status-changed task, invalid stamp, send failure/disconnection, error, duplicate click, reopen and disposal. Gate at repo root on Windows: cmd /d /c "cd /d moe-jetbrains && gradlew.bat test"; Unix: cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test. Reuse the headless JUnit approach, require nonzero counts and red-on-old evidence; serialize shared Gradle outputs.
definitionOfDone: JUnit on the production-used presenter proves the token sent is the successfully rendered revision, never the latest cached one; reopening renders/captures the new revision.

A revision update with unchanged comments invalidates before debounce/early return, shows the refresh notice and prevents even a forced approval action; comment-only same-revision updates stay usable.
Deleted task, changed status, malformed revision or disconnected service cannot send an approval; repeated/pending clicks send at most once, asserted against captured outgoing command.
Send failure or daemon error retains usable failure feedback without reporting approval success; state transitions and disposed callbacks are handled without stale sends or leaked listeners/timers.
Fresh Gradle test exits 0 with nonzero JUnit counts, with scoped red-on-old regression evidence and no unrelated approval entry-point changes.
taskRails: Use disable-and-reopen UX, not partial plan rendering or automatic approval of a newer cached revision.
Never equate transport send success to daemon acceptance.
Consume the centralized steps-plus-DoD revision contract, including in-place mutations; daemon stamping implementation belongs to the producer, not this UI slice.

implementationPlan.description: CREATE THE HEADLESS PRESENTER AND ITS MESSAGE KEYS. New file moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewApprovalState.kt holding the entire approval decision machine with NO Swing, IntelliJ or service imports - that is what makes it drivable by plain JUnit and what keeps it independent of slice 3's exact API. Declare the data types on the OUTER class body, never inside a companion object. Shape: `class PlanReviewApprovalState(private val taskId: String)` plus `data class TaskSnapshot(val present: Boolean, val status: String?, val revision: RevisionToken)`; a sealed `RevisionToken` with `Present(value: Long)`, `LegacyMissing` and `Malformed`; a sealed `Decision` with `Send(taskId: String, expectedPlanRevision: Long)` and `Blocked(messageKey: String)`; and an enum `Phase { AWAITING_RENDER, READY, PENDING, INVALIDATED, FINISHED, DISPOSED }`. The presenter owns exactly one policy rule about tokens: LegacyMissing is the effective revision 0 and is approvable, Malformed is never approvable. Transitions, every one of them synchronized because onState can arrive off the event dispatch thread while the action reads on it: `onRendered(snapshot)` is called ONLY after the Definition of Done and steps panels rendered without throwing, and captures the revision - a Malformed or absent-task or non-AWAITING_APPROVAL snapshot leaves the presenter blocked with a reason key and never captures. `onStateUpdate(snapshot)` returns whether the UI must change and moves to INVALIDATED when the task vanished, its status left AWAITING_APPROVAL, or its revision differs from the captured one - with the single exception that a PENDING approval observing status WORKING becomes FINISHED, which is the ONLY way an approval completes. `onApproveClicked(connected: Boolean, snapshot: TaskSnapshot)` is the independent action-time recheck: it returns Send ONLY from phase READY with connected true, the task present, the status still AWAITING_APPROVAL and the snapshot revision equal to the CAPTURED one, and the Send always carries the captured revision, never the snapshot's newer value; anything else returns Blocked with a specific key, and a successful Send moves to PENDING so a second click is Blocked. `onSendFailed()` and `onDaemonError(operation, message)` return PENDING to READY so the dialog stays open and usable - neither ever reaches FINISHED, because transport success is not daemon acceptance. `onDisposed()` is terminal and makes every later callback a no-op. Expose read-only `approveEnabled` and `noticeKey` for the dialog to apply. Every Blocked key must be a distinct constant so a test can tell the causes apart. Add the matching keys to moe-jetbrains/src/main/resources/messages/MoeBundle.properties in the existing moe.message.* block, including the invalidation notice worded as a close-and-reopen instruction, plus keys for not connected, task missing, status changed, unusable revision, approval already in flight, send failed and daemon error with a parameter for the message. Documented error handling: the presenter never throws for bad input - an unusable snapshot is a Blocked decision, not an exception - because it runs inside Swing callbacks where a throw would leave the dialog wedged.
implementationPlan.note:
Presenter + message keys landed. `gradlew.bat compileKotlin -q` exits 0 with no output (Gradle serialized under the `jetbrains-gradle` lease, acquired 12:37:24Z).

New `PlanReviewApprovalState.kt` (243 lines, longest function 26 lines): zero Swing/IntelliJ/service imports — the only import is `com.moe.model.MAX_SAFE_PLAN_REVISION`, a plain Kotlin const that MoeJsonTest already exercises headlessly. Every DTO sits on the OUTER class body (companion holds only consts and two @JvmStatic functions), per gotcha-kotlin-companion-nested-class.

Decisions worth flagging beyond the plan text:
- `tokenOf(planRevision: Long?)` is the dialog-facing mapper, so LegacyMissing is production-reachable rather than dead: null -> Malformed, 0L -> LegacyMissing, else Present(v). It ALSO folds an out-of-range value to Malformed, because `MoeCommandSender.approveTask` throws IllegalArgumentException outside 0..MAX and the presenter's contract is "never hands the dialog a decision that explodes".
- Click-time staleness LATCHES to INVALIDATED (a plan that changed will not un-change), but `connected == false` does NOT latch — disconnection is transient and a retry has to stay possible. That asymmetry is deliberate and tested next step.
- `onApproveClicked` returns the LATCHED notice key when already INVALIDATED, so the forced-action message names the real cause (task missing / status changed / unusable revision) instead of a generic one.
- `onDaemonError` does not filter on `operation`: any daemon error while PENDING is read as "this approval did not happen". Re-arming a reviewer whose approval did land is a visible annoyance; reporting a success that never happened is a silent lie.
- 11 keys, all distinct constants, enumerated by `allMessageKeys()` for the guard test. Two beyond the plan's list (`alreadyApproved` for a click after FINISHED, `notRendered` for a click before capture) so no reachable Blocked cause shares a key.

11 `moe.message.planReview.*` values appended to MoeBundle.properties, LF endings to match that file (the Kotlin file is CRLF to match its siblings), pure ASCII with `-` never an em dash — java.util.Properties.load decodes ISO-8859-1 and the guard test reads values back. The 18 peer `moe.blocker.*` lines already dirty in that file were left untouched above mine.

implementationPlan.description: COVER THE PRESENTER WITH HEADLESS JUNIT. New file moe-jetbrains/src/test/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewApprovalStateTest.kt, JUnit 4 in the MetricsPanelTest style: no IntelliJ fixture, no Swing, no daemon. Every test asserts an exact value - a specific Decision subtype, a specific message key constant, a specific captured revision - never a bare truthiness check. Required cases, one per Definition of Done item. Rendered capture: after onRendered with revision 7, a click at revision 7 yields Send with expectedPlanRevision 7; after an update to revision 8 the click never yields Send and never carries 8, which is the core 'token sent is the rendered revision, never the latest cached one' proof. Reopen: a FRESH presenter rendered at revision 8 sends 8, modelling close-and-reopen. Identical comments: an update carrying a NEW revision but unchanged comments still invalidates - this is the case the dialog's old early return swallowed, so it is asserted at the presenter level and again at the dialog level in the next step. Same revision with changed comments leaves the presenter READY and approvable. Forced action while invalidated returns Blocked, proving a caller that ignores the disabled button still cannot send. Deleted task, status moved off AWAITING_APPROVAL, Malformed revision and connected false each return their own distinct Blocked key and no Send. Legacy: LegacyMissing renders and sends effective revision 0. Duplicate clicks: two clicks produce exactly one Send, asserted by collecting every returned Decision into a list and checking the list, which is the captured-outgoing-command assertion the Definition of Done asks for. Transport: onSendFailed returns to READY, a retry sends once more, and the presenter is never FINISHED from a send result alone. Daemon error: onDaemonError while PENDING returns to READY with a usable failure key and no approval. Authoritative finish: only a PENDING presenter observing status WORKING reaches FINISHED. Disposal: after onDisposed every callback is inert and no Send is ever produced, proving no stale send after the dialog closed. Concurrency: drive onStateUpdate and onApproveClicked from two threads against one presenter and assert at most one Send total. Add one guard test that loads /messages/MoeBundle.properties from the test classpath with java.util.Properties and asserts every message key the presenter can emit is actually defined, so a missing localization is a test failure rather than a runtime placeholder. Run `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` (Windows: `cmd /d /c "cd /d moe-jetbrains && gradlew.bat test"`) and require green with nonzero counts.

implementationPlan.description: WIRE THE DIALOG TO THE PRESENTER. Edit moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/toolwindow/PlanReviewDialog.kt only. (a) Hold a PlanReviewApprovalState built from task.id, and add a notice label to the header area that is hidden until the presenter reports a notice key. (b) Capture after render, not before: at the END of createCenterPanel, once createDodPanel and createStepsPanel have both returned, call onRendered with a snapshot built from the current task; wrap the render in try/catch so a rendering failure logs and leaves the presenter uncaptured and the approve button disabled - failing closed is the required error handling here, since an unrendered plan was never reviewed. (c) In onState, call the presenter FIRST - immediately after `task = updated` and strictly BEFORE the `if (oldComments == newComments) return` early return and before any debounce scheduling - and when it reports a change, apply it in its own SwingUtilities.invokeLater that disables the approve action and shows the notice. That invokeLater must not be inside the debounce timer, or a revision change arriving with identical comments would never reach the screen. Leave the existing comment debounce exactly as it is for same-revision comment updates. (d) Replace the approve action body: build a fresh snapshot from service.getState() at click time, pass it with service.isConnected() to onApproveClicked, and act on the Decision - Send calls the service with the captured revision and then does NOTHING else, no close, because transport success is not approval; Blocked shows the localized message and keeps the dialog open. Disable the approve action while pending so a repeated click cannot send twice even if the button is somehow re-armed. (e) If the delivered service call reports a send result, feed a failure into onSendFailed; override onError(operation, message) to feed onDaemonError, re-enabling the action and showing the existing message unchanged. (f) Close with OK_EXIT_CODE only when the presenter reaches FINISHED, which happens only from observed authoritative state. (g) In dispose, call onDisposed BEFORE stopping the debounce timer and removing the listener, so nothing queued can send after teardown; keep the existing timer stop, pendingUpdate clear and removeListener. Change nothing in createDodPanel, createStepsPanel, renderComments, the reject action or the ask-a-question path, and do not touch the four unrelated approval entry points named in step 1.
implementationPlan.note:
Dialog wired to the machine; +150/-10 in one file. `gradlew.bat test --rerun` BUILD SUCCESSFUL, exit 0 (counts re-verified in step 5).

Wiring points, in the order the Definition of Done cares about:
(b) `createCenterPanel` now builds the container, calls `buildReviewContent` inside try/catch, and calls `approval.onRendered(snapshotOf(task))` as the LAST statement of the try — after createDodPanel and createStepsPanel returned. A render that throws is logged and leaves the machine uncaptured, so the button stays disabled: an unrendered plan was never reviewed. `applyApprovalState()` runs outside the try so the button state is applied on both paths.
(c) `onState` calls `approval.onStateUpdate(...)` immediately after the lookup and BEFORE `if (updated == null) return`, before the comments-equality return and outside the debounce; a reported change gets its OWN `SwingUtilities.invokeLater`, never the 200ms Timer. The existing comment debounce is byte-identical for same-revision comment updates.
(d) The approve action reads `service.getState()?.tasks?.find { it.id == task.id }` fresh at click time and passes it with `service.isConnected()`. Send calls `service.approveTask(send.taskId, send.expectedPlanRevision)` and does NOT close; Blocked shows the localized cause and keeps the dialog open.
(e) `service.approveTask` returning false feeds `onSendFailed()`; a throw is caught, logged and treated as not-delivered (defence in depth — `tokenOf` already folds an out-of-range stamp to Malformed so the `require` in MoeCommandSender is unreachable from here). `onError(operation, message)` is overridden and feeds `onDaemonError`.
(f) `close(OK_EXIT_CODE)` exists in exactly one place — `applyApprovalState()` when the phase is FINISHED, which only observed authoritative state can produce.
(g) `dispose()` calls `approval.onDisposed()` FIRST, then the untouched timer stop / pendingUpdate clear / removeListener.

Two structural notes for the reviewer. First, `createCenterPanel`'s body moved verbatim into `buildReviewContent` + `buildCommentsSection` rather than being wrapped in place: that keeps each function under the 50-line cap and keeps the try/catch scope honest. The ask-a-question path, renderComments, createDodPanel, createStepsPanel and the reject action are unchanged apart from that move; `add(noticeLabel)` is the only new line in the header. Second, the notice is a JBLabel, which is safe ONLY because it is always fed `MoeBundle.message(key, lastErrorMessage)` — the daemon's arbitrary text can never lead the string, and a JLabel renders HTML only when the text STARTS with an html tag (gotcha-jetbrains-headless-presentation-bundle-keys item 3).

Deliberate conservatism: `service.getState()` returning null makes the snapshot `present=false`, so a click blocks with taskMissing. "Cannot verify" is refusal, not approval. The four unrelated approval entry points, and everything in VS Code, are untouched.

implementationPlan.description: RED-ON-OLD EVIDENCE AND THE FULL GATE. The presenter is a new file, so 'fails on the old behaviour' is proven by mutation rather than by running the new test against an empty tree - restore the checkout after each mutation and verify with a separate git status call, never trusting the edit alone. Perform and record at least these four, naming the exact tests that fail for each: move the presenter call in onState to AFTER the comments-equality early return, which must break the new-revision-with-identical-comments case; make onApproveClicked send the snapshot's current revision instead of the captured one, which must break the rendered-token case and is the precise defect this task exists to fix; delete the PENDING guard so a duplicate click sends twice, which must break the at-most-one-Send assertion; and treat a successful send as approval by reaching FINISHED from onSendFailed's sibling path, which must break the transport-is-not-acceptance case. Then run the gate clean from the repo root - Windows `cmd /d /c "cd /d moe-jetbrains && gradlew.bat test"`, Unix `cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew test` - and require exit 0 with nonzero JUnit counts and no regression in the existing MetricsPanelTest, CreateTaskDialogTest, MoeSettingsDialogTest, MoeJsonTest or the services tests. Gradle output is a shared resource on this box: serialize it through the Moe resource protocol rather than running concurrently with another agent's Gradle build, and do not clean a peer's cache. Keep the exact command, exit code and counts for the verification argument of moe.complete_task, and keep the mutation evidence for QA.

implementationPlan.description: ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, THEN HAND OFF. implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial pass done; 2 real findings fixed, gate re-run green (14 classes / 186 tests / 0 failures / 0 errors / 0 skipped, XML 15:47:46, exit 0).

FIXED — (1) `lastErrorMessage` was written on the daemon message thread in onError and read on the EDT in showNotice with no memory barrier; now `@Volatile`. (2) An arbitrary-length daemon error string landed whole in a header label; now `message.take(MAX_ERROR_CHARS)` (300).

CHECKED AND CLEAN, each traced through the code:
- Identical-comments revision change reaches the screen: onStateUpdate runs before the `updated == null` guard, before the comments-equality return and outside the debounce, with its own invokeLater. Pinned by the source-order guard test and proven red by mutation M1.
- Captured token on every path: `Decision.Send` is constructed only from `capturedRevision`; `snapshot` is used for comparison only. After N updates the capture is unchanged (test at 7 -> 8 -> 9 -> 10). M2 red proves the substitution is caught.
- No close on transport success: `close(OK_EXIT_CODE)` appears once in applyApprovalState gated on FINISHED, once in the pre-existing reject path. The approve action contains no close at all (guard test asserts it; M5 red). FINISHED is reachable only from PENDING observing WORKING.
- Disconnected / deleted / status-moved / unusable revision: each returns its own Blocked key with no call to `service.approveTask`. `getState()` returning null is also a refusal (present=false), because "cannot verify" is not "approve".
- At most one send: the PENDING guard plus one lock; 50-iteration two-thread test; M3 red.
- After dispose: onDisposed runs first, every later callback is inert, the timer is stopped, pendingUpdate cleared, the listener removed. A send in flight at dispose cannot repaint (onSendFailed returns false when not PENDING).
- The machine cannot throw into a Swing callback: no throw statement, no `!!`, no unchecked cast, arithmetic-free; every unusable input is a Blocked decision.
- Every message key resolves: 11 keys walked against the bundle by the guard test. Checked the MessageFormat traps too — no apostrophe and no stray brace in any new value (BundleBase runs the value through MessageFormat whenever params are passed, and an apostrophe would silently eat the rest), and all values are pure ASCII so the Properties-based guard reads them identically to the platform's UTF-8 read.
- Scope: `git status` shows exactly 4 JetBrains paths. `git diff` on ApproveTaskAction.kt, MoeToolWindowPanel.kt and TaskDetailDialog.kt is 0 lines. No line in the PlanReviewDialog diff touches rejectTask, addTaskComment, renderComments, createDodPanel or createStepsPanel. Nothing from moe-vscode or the daemon; no Wave 1 concepts.

NOTED, NOT FIXED (theoretical, for QA):
- `task` is assigned on the daemon thread and read on the EDT without synchronization. Pre-existing behaviour, unchanged by this task, and harmless for approval: only `task.id` is used there and the id never changes. Out of scope to fix here.
- If another client approves the task while our send is in flight, we can emit one redundant APPROVE_TASK carrying our captured revision to a task that already moved. The daemon refuses it; no false success is reportable, since only observed state finishes an approval.
- `applyApprovalState()` is called unguarded inside doAction and at the end of createCenterPanel. It can only throw via MoeBundle, which returns a placeholder rather than throwing for a missing key, and the key-coverage test makes a missing key a build failure.

HONEST BOUNDARY (also in the completion summary): this binds the JetBrains review dialog to the plan it rendered. The daemon-side compare-and-swap in sibling task-dd743a02000e46cca6ae2442a1821066 is what actually REFUSES a stale token; a client that omits `expectedPlanRevision` still takes the legacy path, and automatic SPEED/TURBO approvals are unchanged by design. VS Code parity is a separate card.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Putting the decision logic directly in PlanReviewDialog and testing it through an IntelliJ fixture - rejected: the existing suite is headless plain JUnit, and a DialogWrapper test needs a platform fixture the build deliberately strips arguments for. (2) Having the presenter depend on the Task model and the service - rejected: slice 3 is not landed yet, so binding the presenter to its types would make this whole slice unbuildable and untestable until that lands; a presenter over plain values keeps slice 3's API confined to a handful of dialog lines. (3) Re-rendering the plan in place when the revision changes - rejected by a task rail: the required UX is latch-disabled plus a close-and-reopen notice, because a partial re-render is exactly how a reviewer ends up approving something they never read. (4) Comparing a client-side hash of the rendered steps and Definition of Done - rejected by the task comment: the daemon's centralized revision already covers in-place mutations, so a second client-side notion of freshness would drift. (5) Closing the dialog on send success - rejected: transport success is not daemon acceptance, so only an observed status move finishes an approval. (6) Returning localized strings from the presenter - rejected: it returns stable message keys so it stays free of IntelliJ imports and the tests can assert exact causes.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The stale-render hole is concrete and visible: onState assigns `task = updated` and then returns early when comments are equal, so a plan whose steps or Definition of Done changed silently replaces the reviewed task object while the screen keeps showing the old plan, and the approve action then sends for whatever task.id holds. The approve action also closes on OK_EXIT_CODE the instant it calls the service, so a send that never left the socket looks exactly like an approval. MoeStateListener.onError already exists as a defaulted interface method routed from real daemon ERROR frames, so daemon-side refusals are observable without touching the service layer. MoeCommandSender.approveTask currently swallows its own ensureConnected result, which is precisely the send-result gap that prerequisite slice 3 owns. There are four other approval entry points (ApproveTaskAction:17, MoeToolWindowPanel:511 and :570, TaskDetailDialog:580) that this task must leave alone, which only works if slice 3 gave the revision parameter a default. Kotlin trap already paid for once in this repo: a class nested inside a companion object is not importable as Outer.Inner, so shared data types go on the outer class body. Main resources are on the test runtime classpath, so a plain JUnit test can load /messages/MoeBundle.properties and assert key coverage without any IntelliJ fixture.
planningNotes.risks: Ordering inside onState is the whole defect: any presenter call placed after the comments-equality return, or any notice applied inside the debounce timer, reintroduces exactly the bug being fixed - assert it behaviorally, and prove it by mutation. The presenter is touched from both the state callback and the event dispatch thread, so every transition must be synchronized or a duplicate send becomes a real race rather than a theoretical one. Never let the click substitute the snapshot's newer revision for the captured one; that is the single most likely wrong implementation because it makes the naive test pass. The revision must stay a safe Long end to end - do not narrow it to Int anywhere. A legacy row with no stamp is approvable as effective 0, but a malformed stamp is never approvable, so those two states must not collapse into one nullable value. If slice 3 made the revision parameter required rather than defaulted, four unrelated approval entry points would stop compiling and the file scope would blow past four - stop and report instead of widening. Gradle output is a shared resource here: serialize it, and do not clean a peer's cache. The bundle keys must exist or the UI shows a raw placeholder at exactly the moment a reviewer needs the warning, which is why a key-coverage test is part of the suite. Do not touch VS Code or Wave 1, and do not claim this slice alone prevents stale approvals - the daemon compare-and-swap in the sibling task is what refuses a stale token.
